label: copy phase: outputting (or about to output) a, esp. a; also v/w/q/s
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L; essentially never in the original or delimiter steps). It is selective for the token being output, with a strong preference for a (60% of steps outputting a are active, 13.8x lift, 35% of mass), then v, w, q, s (4-6x lift), and weaker graded preferences for c, n, l, d, y, k. It also fires one step before an a is output (next_out == a, 8.3x lift). The largest activations come at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, right after <DEL>) when the sequence is ...a a... (e.g. z a a a a w l -> 1.0 on the step outputting the first a, then decaying across the following a outputs). Magnitude falls with later recall positions. Many weak activations fall on other output tokens early in the copy phase, so precision is limited (dev P 0.36, R 0.65, mass recall 0.77). Simpler out_tok==a or next_out==a: P 0.63, mass recall 0.51.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: a, v, w, q, s, c; least: -, z, 2, h) and the next token to output (most: a, w, q, s, l, y; least: 3, j, 2, h); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, recall_idx=1, recall_idx=3.
